Theme

School & learning

gender noun

in grammar

also genders, grammatical gender, what gender is it?

classical

Varr. LL 10.22: dīrēctōrum genera (Lewis & Short: “in gram., gender”)
Quint. 1.4.23: trādere in nōminibus tria genera
Traupman 221, 246

genus, generis n.

noun, third declension

grammatical gender; in verbs, voice

Nouns have three genders, genus masculīnum, fēminīnum, neutrum (Traupman 221). The question goes in the genitive of description: Cujus generis est?, what gender is it?, answered Fēminīnī (Traupman 238). With verbs the same word means voice (see voice).

Examples

  • nōn erit contentus trādere in nōminibus tria genera et quae sunt duōbus omnibusve commūnia

    he will not be content to teach the three genders of nouns and those common to two or to allQuint. 1.4.23

  • Cujus est generis?

    What gender is it?Traupman 239

  • Genera nōminum quot sunt?

    How many genders do nouns have?Traupman 221

See also masculine, feminine, neuter, noun, voice, sex.

SourcesLewis & Short: genus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 221, 238, 246.
